opening.headline: The problem of uploading a file but not reflecting it in the answer is resolved by determining how the uploaded file is used and how to check it.
body: I uploaded a product FAQ document to the project and asked how long the refund period would be, and I received a general answer. The FAQ is clearly visible in the file list. The fact that it was posted and the fact that it was used in the answer are two different things.

In this class, we will first summarize the role of files uploaded to the ChatGPT project, GPT, Claude project, and Gemini's Gem. Next, you will learn how to distinguish between cases where the entire file is included in the context and cases where only the necessary fragments are retrieved and written, and how to check whether the response came from the file. At the end, we unravel the process of identifying the causes of cases where the FAQ is reflected in only some questions, one by one.

You can identify the reason why a file is not reflected in the answer.

First, let's look at a situation where the answer doesn't change even though you uploaded the file. Read where expectations and results misalign.

visual.alt: A response that seems unrelated to the list of uploaded files on the left and the files on the right.
labels: How many days is the refund period?
Usually between a week and a month

paragraphs: A product FAQ document has been uploaded to the project. However, when I asked how many days the refund period would be, I received an answer similar to the general refund policy rather than what is written in the FAQ. This is true even though the FAQ is clearly visible in the file list.

What's more troubling is that it's inconsistent. Some questions reflect the file contents, some do not. The fact that it was posted and the fact that it was used in the answer are two different things.
The question for this class is this. How are uploaded files used, and what should I suspect if they are not reflected?

screens.outro: First, let me recall your experience.

screens.title: After uploading a file, have you ever checked to see if the contents of the file appeared in the reply?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You will not enter or submit your answer, so think first before clicking.

items.prompt: Have you ever uploaded a file and checked to see if it was cited in the response?
items.answer: Many people end up uploading files. However, you won't know if the file was written unless you see the file's sentence or source in the response. For products that require citations, citations are the easiest clue.

items.prompt: Has your assistant ever given a plausible answer to something that wasn't in the file?
items.answer: If so, the answer likely came from general knowledge rather than the file. Just because it's a plausible answer doesn't mean it's based on the file. This is why we need instructions to say that there is nothing in the file that is not there.

items.prompt: How do you know if a file is being used if you don't check it?
items.answer: I don't know. So this lesson covers file reference resolution as one step. We'll soon see how to look at quote marks, or ask for numbers and unique terms that only exist in a file to see if they come out exactly as they are.

screens.outro: Now that we've summarized our experience, let's start by looking at what a knowledge file is.

screens.title: Knowledge files: supporting evidence, not guidance
screens.lead: Select each tab to see where and how to upload files from the three companies' products. Notice that the instructions and knowledge are divided.

visual.alt: Illustration of the instruction box on the left and the knowledge file drawer on the right being referenced together in one conversation.
labels: Knowledge file (what to base it on)
Rules of Directive + Basis of File

tabs.label: OpenAI
tabs.body: To the ChatGPT project, you can upload PDFs, spreadsheets, documents, images, or paste text to use as reference material. The number of files you can upload varies depending on your plan. In GPT, you upload a file to Knowledge and let GPT utilize its contents. GPT guidance explains that knowledge is appropriate for reference materials such as documents, guides, and handbooks, and distinguishes between rules and actions to be written down in guidance. If you write rules to a file without observing this distinction, they may not always be applied.

tabs.label: Anthropic
tabs.body: Claude projects upload documents, text files, and code snippets to the knowledge area on the right side of the screen. The uploaded data will be used in all chats of the project. Conversely, context between chats is not automatically shared, so information needed from multiple chats must be put into knowledge. Knowledge and guidance are separate, so data is placed in knowledge and methods of action are placed in guidance.

tabs.label: Google
tabs.body: After writing the instructions, Gem uploads the file by clicking Add files in the knowledge section. You can upload it from your device or add it from Drive, and since Gemini uses the most recent version of Drive files, any modifications to the original will be reflected in Gem. Citations for uploaded files can be turned off in settings. Gemini Notebook is a research aid that uses uploaded data as a basis, and informs you that responses will be accompanied by citations pointing to the source.

tabs.label: common principles
tabs.body: For all three products, files are reference materials and guidelines are rules that dictate behavior. Uploading a file does not automatically add all the answers, but only the parts needed depending on the question. So, if you uploaded a file, it would be a good idea to include a line in the instructions telling you to base your answer on this data.

screens.outro: Now that we know where the data is located, let's look at two ways the file actually enters the response.

screens.title: Search-based usage and direct entry into context
screens.lead: Switch between small and large files and compare how the file is used in the response changes.

visual.alt: A two-pronged diagram showing where the question takes the relevant fragment from the file and where the entire file goes into the window.
labels: Large files: Search uses only fragments
Find fragments related to your question

states.label: small file
states.body: Smaller files ensure that the entire content is included in the context of the conversation. Every time your assistant is asked a question, it's looking at the entire file, so it's less likely to miss relevant content if the question is worded differently than in the file. Instead, there is a limit to the context, so the more a file occupies the context, the less space there is for conversations and responses. Short FAQs or one- or two-page policy documents are most often written this way.

states.label: big file
states.body: If there are many or large files, it can be used as a search basis. This method finds only the pieces related to the question and reflects them in the answer. Project Claude notes that on paid plans, when knowledge approaches the context limit, it automatically turns on RAG mode, increasing capacity by up to 10x. The weakness of this approach is that if the wording of the question is far from the wording of the file, relevant fragments may be missed. So, if you use the terminology of the file in the question or write where to look in the instructions, the reflection rate will increase.

screens.outro: Now that you know the difference between the methods, let's see how to check if the response came from a file.

screens.title: Check file references: Visually check if they are reflected
screens.lead: In the sample responses below, select one by one the highlighted passages. An explanation of how each phrase is used to check whether it reflects the file or not appears.

data.text:
[Question] How many days do I have to request a refund?
[Answer] You can request a refund within 14 days from the date of purchase. [1]
[Source 1] Product FAQ.pdf: "The grace period for returns is 14 days from the date of purchase."

[Verification Question] What is the warranty period for product code HB-2207?
[Answer] The warranty period is 24 months. [2]
[Source 2] Product FAQ.pdf: Line HB-2207 of Warranty Table

marks.note: This is the quote number in the response. Gemini Notebook informs you that a citation indicating the source is attached to the response so that you can check which source it came from. Press the number to match the source passage with the response sentence.

marks.span: Product FAQ.pdf: "The grace period for returns is 14 days from the date of purchase."
marks.note: Place the response sentence and the file passage side by side to see if they are the same. If there are no citations or the content differs from the passage, you may suspect that the file was not written. Gem has a setting to turn off knowledge citation, so it's easy to check if you turn it on.

marks.span: What is the warranty period for product code HB-2207?
marks.note: This is a confirmation question. Ask for numbers or unique terms that only exist in the file and see if the values ​​are returned as they are. To be meaningful, a question must be one that cannot be answered with general knowledge.

Since the values found only in the file came out as is and quotations were added, it can be determined that the file was used. If the values ​​in the same question are incorrect or seem made up, it is a sign that the file was not reflected.
This is how you check whether the values in the table have been read. If you cannot read the table, the results will vary, with only the values ​​in the sentences outside the table being correct.

screens.outro: Now that you have learned how to check, let's work with the instructor to solve cases that are not reflected.

screens.title: Explanation: Why the product FAQ reflects only some questions
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow the instructor as he or she confirms or excludes candidate causes one by one.

visual.alt: A side-by-side illustration of some of the FAQs on the left and a table of responses to each question and candidate causes on the right.
labels: The grace period for returns is 14 days from the date of purchase.
Question about shipping cost when exchanging: Not reflected (X)

steps.title: Check case
steps.body: A product FAQ has been posted to the project. If you ask about the refund period, the FAQ content is reflected, but if you ask about the shipping cost for exchange, it is not reflected and a general answer is given. Since it is the same file, it is not a problem that the file cannot be read at all. Find out for each candidate why only some questions fail.

steps.title: Candidate cause 1: Inconsistency in expression
steps.body: The FAQ says it's a deferred return, not an exchange. If the file is large, relevant fragments are found based on search, but if the wording of the question is far from the wording of the file, relevant fragments may be missed. The refund period question is reflected because it is close to the wording of the file, and the exchange question seems to be missed because it is far away. This is the most likely candidate.

steps.title: Candidate Cause 2: Layout
steps.body: If shipping cost information is included in a table, it may not be read well as text. GPT instructions recommend text-oriented files rather than complex layouts. Open the file to see if the content is in a table or image. In this case, the shipping cost is in the table, so it remains a candidate.

steps.title: Candidate Cause 3: Missing Instructions
steps.body: If the instructions don't tell you to base your answer on the FAQ, your assistant can base your answer on general knowledge. Questions with similar files and general knowledge, such as refund period, may seem coincidental. When I opened the instructions and checked, there was no sentence about using evidence.

steps.title: Candidate cause 4: Duplicate files
steps.body: If old files with the same name exist together, the contents may be mixed or old values may appear. When I checked the file list, there was another FAQ from an older version.

steps.title: organizing
steps.body: In this case, there wasn't just one cause, but all four candidates were involved to some extent. The biggest inconsistencies in wording were overlapping layouts, missing instructions, and duplicate files. Rather than assuming a single cause, the method is to check the candidates in order.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the cause, let's look at the steps to fix it.

screens.title: Explanation: Procedure for fixing files that are not reflected
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to apply the corrections one by one and see how the answers to the failed questions change.

steps.title: Step 1: Solve the contents of the table into sentences
steps.body: Create a new file with the shipping cost table written in paragraph form. For example, when exchanging, the shipping cost is borne by the seller if the product is defective, and the customer is borne by the customer if he or she simply changes his or her mind. Re-uploading as a text-centric file increases the chances of your content being read.

steps.title: Step 2: Get the terms right
steps.body: The term for the file, deferred return, and the term for the question, exchange, are written together in the FAQ. For example, you can write deferred returns (including exchanges). If two expressions are in one sentence, asking either way will retrieve the related fragment.

steps.title: Step 3: Write Evidence Use in Guidelines
steps.body: Add to the guidelines the following: Product inquiries will be answered based on the uploaded FAQ, and if there is none, say there is none. This way, instead of answering based on general knowledge, you look for the FAQ first, and if you can't find it, you say you don't know.

steps.title: Step 4: Organize old files
steps.body: Old files with the same name are deleted. ChatGPT lets you choose between Upload anyway and Skip when uploading files with the same name, so make sure there are no unintentional duplicates when uploading again.

steps.title: recheck
steps.body: Finally, re-ask the two questions that failed the first time to see if the citation sticks. Both refund period questions and shipping cost questions for exchanges are resolved by quoting passages from the FAQ. The GPT instructions also instruct you to upload the file and check whether it is used as intended in Preview.

screens.outro: Now that we've confirmed the repair order, let's summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaways
screens.lead: Summarizes the contents of this class. As you read, try to answer the initial question: how the file is used and what you suspect when it doesn't reflect it.

paragraphs: The first question was how the uploaded file is used and what to suspect when it is not reflected. You need to make sure that files are not only uploaded, but utilized. In small files, the entire content is put into context, and in large files, only the fragments relevant to the question are retrieved.

Whether or not it is reflected is checked by citation marks and confirmation questions asking for numbers or unique terms found only in the file. The instructions note how and in what format you will answer based on the file.

If it is not reflected, we suspect a mismatch in the wording of the question and the file, a complex layout such as a table, missing sentences using the basis for the instructions, and duplicate files with the same name in the order. After making corrections, check again by asking the question that failed the first time.

Think back to the FAQ from the first scene. Just showing the file in the file list was not enough, and the file could be used as an assistant through a process of matching the wording of the question, writing down the basis for use in the instructions, and checking the citation.

The same check can be done anywhere in ChatGPT's project, GPT, Claude project, or Gem. Every time you upload a file, you can set two or three representative questions and one value that is unique to the file. If you check with the same question immediately after uploading and immediately after changing the file, you can quickly find out whether it is reflected or not.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: The point is not to upload the file, but to make sure it is utilized. Get into the habit of checking with quotation marks and values ​​that only exist in the file.

glossary.def: This is reference material that the assistant can use as a basis for its answers. Rules and actions are placed in instructions and rationale is placed in knowledge files.
When there are many or large files, only fragments related to the question are found and reflected in the answer. Also known as RAG.
This is a case where the file is small and the entire content is included in the context of the conversation.
The task is to check whether the response came from the file through quotation marks and values found only in the file.

misconceptions.myth: Once a file is uploaded, it is always read.
misconceptions.fact: When search-based, only fragments matching the question are used, so you must check whether they are reflected.

misconceptions.myth: If you write rules in a file, they are followed like guidelines.
misconceptions.fact: Knowledge is the reference, rules and tone are the guidelines.

misconceptions.myth: If the answer is plausible, the file has been written.
misconceptions.fact: If there is no citation and something is not in the file, the answer may come from general knowledge. Check with citations and file unique values.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: The point is not to upload the file, but to make sure it is utilized.
Small files go directly into the context, and large files are fragmented by searches.
Check whether it is reflected based on quotation marks and values found only in the file.
If it is not reflected, I suspect it is in the presentation, layout, instructions, or duplicate file order.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What questions can I ask to see if the knowledge I upload to my Assistant is actually being used?

checks.q: I posted a product FAQ, but it is not reflected in the 'shipping fee for exchange' question. In the file, the expression ‘return deferment’ is written. What is the most likely cause?
options: This is because the file was changed to instructions and disappeared from the knowledge section.
This is because the file is small and the entire thing is not included in the context.
This is because the question wording is far from the file wording, and related fragments were missed in the search.
This is because if you get the same question wrong once, it will stay wrong.
checks.explain: If there are many or large files, only the fragments related to the question are found and written, but if the expression is far away, it may be missed. If you use the same terminology in questions or FAQs, the reflection rate increases.

wrong.0: Knowledge files do not change into guidelines and do not correspond to the phenomenon of being reflected only in some questions.
wrong.1: If it is a small file, the entire content is placed in context and is difficult to miss.
wrong.3: There is no fixed device for the answer, and it changes if you change the terminology or instructions.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: Please place them in the correct order to fix FAQ files that are not reflected.
items: Repost the contents of the table in paragraph form.
Write file terminology and question terminology together in the FAQ.
Add a sentence to the instructions to answer based on the uploaded FAQ.
Delete old files with the same name
Re-ask the question that failed the first time and see if the citation sticks.
checks.explain: Edit the file itself to make it readable, adjust the terminology, indicate the use of evidence as a guideline, organize the old file, and finally recheck.
checks.intro: Pause for a moment and check your understanding. It will not be submitted or graded.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Unfortunately, this is not the correct answer.
